findings.summary: The snapshot is dropped before the review is written down, so if dropping it panics, the paid review is lost.
findings.detail: `drop_snapshot(&root)` runs right after `review(...)` returns and before the record is read or written. `drop_snapshot` panics on several failures: `git worktree remove --force` failing (goes through `git`, which panics on a non-zero exit), `build_submodules` reading `HEAD:Cargo.toml` from a tree a `--run` reviewer may have changed, or `remove_dir_all(...).unwrap()`. If any of these happens, the run ends with no record and no findings printed, after paying for up to 40 agent turns. The baseline tool writes its output after every run, before it drops the snapshot, so a failed cleanup there loses nothing. Writing the record (and printing the findings) before cleaning up would avoid this.

findings.summary: The `--run` task always grants `$HOME/.cargo` and `$HOME/.rustup`, but the runner uses `$CARGO_HOME` and `$RUSTUP_HOME` whenever they are set.
findings.detail: `home_runner()` sets `cargo_home` to `env("CARGO_HOME")` and `rustup_home` to `env("RUSTUP_HOME")`, falling back to `~/.cargo` and `~/.rustup` only when they are unset. The `eddy-review` task always passes `--process-read "$HOME/.cargo" --process-read "$HOME/.rustup"`. On a machine where either variable points somewhere else, which is common with mise- or CI-managed toolchains, the cargo the reviewer starts cannot read its toolchain or registry, so every Run fails and the `--run` review cannot reproduce anything. The task should grant `${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}` and `${RUSTUP_HOME:-$HOME/.rustup}`.

findings.summary: An existing record file that does not parse makes the run panic after the review, dropping the new review.
findings.detail: The record is read only after the review has finished, with `from_string::<Record, String>(text).unwrap()`. Any `<head>.json` that does not match the current `Record`/`Attempt` shape triggers that panic. That includes a record written by the first commit of this branch, which kept `base` on the record instead of on each attempt, and a file with a merge conflict or a hand edit. The panic happens after the API spend, and neither the new attempt nor the findings are saved or printed. Checking the record before the review, or reporting the parse error without discarding the result, would avoid the loss.
